paragraphs: A live, side-by-side visualization of block-diffusion generation. Describe a game asset (a sword, potion, treasure chest, spaceship, ...) and the model designs an original SVG illustration by denoising a canvas of random tokens — every position updates at once each step. A fixed, hand-written Three.js harness then extrudes that SVG into an interactive, spinning 3D object.

The left pane shows the raw SVG canvas diffusing token-by-token (the signature look of text diffusion); the right pane shows the extruded 3D scene (drag to orbit). Type a follow-up to tweak in place: the previous artwork seeds the diffusion's starting canvas (via the model's native canvasids API), so the model edits the existing asset instead of regenerating from scratch.

repositories.description: One read, every routing decision

paragraphs: Vela 2.0 Studio is a playground for the Vela 2.0 model family by KR Labs and vLLM Semantic Router. One SystemOne request asks several router questions about one state, and the answers include the exact spans behind them.
features: Router in one pass. Paste a request and, optionally, a retrieved context and a model's answer. One request returns safety, jailbreak (Noul), domain and modality (Choice) and urgency (Score). It also marks personal data…
Evidence for RAG. Give a question and the retrieved passages. The same request marks the exact supporting spans (broad span head) and returns router decisions about the question.

Ask your documents. One model for the whole RAG, over a built-in knowledge base of 60 Wikipedia paragraphs about ten famous bridges (CC BY-SA 4.0). Vela 2.0 4B embeds the question and retrieves the top 10, reranks them…

Verbatim RAG. Give a question, up to three retrieved documents and an answer template with {slots}. One request marks the evidence, fills each slot with an exact span of a document, extracts your own labels and checks…

repositories.description: Qwen3.5-4B CPU chat; remote image and video

paragraphs: Text chat runs locally on Hugging Face CPU Basic (2 vCPU, 16 GB RAM). The default model is Huihui-Qwen3.5-4B-abliterated Q4KM, a 2.71 GB GGUF. It replaces the previous 10.2 GB Qwen3.8-27B IQ2M model to reduce response latency. This is a different, smaller model, so its answers and refusal behaviour will differ. It still runs on CPU; replies may remain slower than GPU-hosted chat. The app logs prompt size, time to first token, total time, and reply token count for live speed checks.

The app memory maps the model and serves one generation at a time. The default context is 4,096 tokens including history and reply. Long histories or text attachments may need shortening. Max new tokens = 0 uses the space left in that context.

paragraphs: An OpenEnv environment where AI agents learn to detect, classify, and correct hallucinations in LLM-generated text. Built for the Meta × OpenEnv × Hugging Face × PyTorch Hackathon.

LLM hallucinations — factual errors, fabricated entities, and logical inconsistencies — are one of the biggest barriers to deploying AI in production. According to research, up to 27% of LLM-generated facts can be hallucinated in open-domain tasks. Content moderators, fact-checkers, and AI safety teams manually verify LLM outputs every day.
This environment trains RL agents to be automated hallucination auditors — a task with direct production value:
features: HF Space (Live Demo)
Fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B Model
